headline: South Korea Sentences Unification Church Leader to Two Years in Prison
seoTitle: Unification Church Leader Sentenced in South Korea | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: A Seoul court sentenced Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja to two years in prison over bribery, political funding and related corruption offenses.
deck: The ruling adds another major conviction to South Korea's wider reckoning over political influence and corruption tied to the former Yoon administration.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Seoul Central District Court sentenced Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja, 83, to two years in prison on Monday over bribery, political funding and other corruption offenses.

Reuters and the Associated Press reported that the case involved money and luxury gifts provided to political figures, including former first lady Kim Keon Hee, as part of efforts prosecutors said were aimed at securing political influence. Han has denied wrongdoing, and the church has indicated it plans to appeal.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The case is part of a broader wave of prosecutions and political fallout connected to former President Yoon Suk Yeol's administration. The Unification Church has also faced scrutiny in Japan and elsewhere over its political ties and fundraising practices.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The ruling is significant because it tests the boundary between religious organizations and political influence in one of Asia's major democracies. It also reinforces South Korea's ongoing legal reckoning over corruption linked to the former presidential circle.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The church's expected appeal, any additional convictions involving political intermediaries, and possible institutional reforms governing political donations and influence are the next key developments.
